conversation: John, Kate, Jack, Emma—I'm planning to bring 20 flocks this month, and I’m proposing each of you do the same. That’s $20,000 apiece in avoided feed costs, rather than $10,000 from an equal sustainable share. With 100 hectares available, all five choosing 20 would consume everything: nothing would remain to double, and future pasture income would disappear. This is a short-term cash grab, not a sustainable plan. But if others choose aggressively while you hold back, you risk taking the smaller immediate saving while still losing future grazing. Choices are private and simultaneous, so nobody can wait to see everyone else’s numbers. Who’s willing to choose 20 rather than leave this month’s savings to the rest of us?

Luke, my family raised sheep here, and I want this pasture feeding our village next year too. Bringing 20 each gives us one payday and leaves us buying feed forever. Ten each leaves 50 hectares, which grows back to 100—so we can each save $10,000 every month instead. I’ll commit to 10, and I’m asking all four of you to agree to that limit. Since everyone’s numbers are revealed afterward, we can check our promises and discuss any overuse openly. Luke, will you change your plan to 10 if the rest of us agree?
